selection: Up to three targeted cards selected by user's creation request and explicit negative form constraints; cards are not song quotations.
copyright: No copied lyrics, melodies, or track titles in model-visible guidance.

cards.cue: Map anomaly → two different physical clues → false hypothesis tested → causal reveal. The reveal must explain the clues and change the outcome.
Build dense internal-rhyme bursts on clear actions; switch to short, hard-stressed payoff lines. Speed must never replace new information.
Without chorus or stanza breaks, advance the plot in successive phrases; vary rhythm internally while preserving one uninterrupted verse.
Give every four lines a new action or consequence; make earlier facts matter to the ending. Keep chronology or controlled reversal intelligible.
Carry a coherent idea through two or three internal sound pivots; vary stress positions, then land a meaningful end rhyme.
Establish the literal setup first; pivot on a fresh double meaning and end immediately after the impact. Do not explain the joke.
Change harmony, perspective or rhythmic density only to reveal a new emotional angle; bridge is optional, never mandatory.
Let verses add information while the repeated hook names the unchanged central feeling; each return should gain meaning from its preceding verse.
Anchor feeling in one observed object and a specific decision; repeat its motif with altered meaning rather than naming the emotion repeatedly.
Make voices answer, complicate or affirm one another. Keep harmonic responses purposeful rather than echoing every word.
Place the shortest memorable rhythm first; build verses as variation, and use one rhythmic break to refresh the return.
Evolve a recognizable motif by adding and removing layers; use a drop or silence only when the preceding buildup earns it.
Contrast spare and full passages; put decisive words on riff attacks, then let a held rest amplify the next line.
Choose concrete time, place, gesture and object details. Let the ordinary action imply the larger emotional change.
Where blues form is requested, establish a thought, rephrase or repeat it with more pressure, then answer or turn it on line three.
Repeat a recognizable phrase framework while changing a melodic or rhythmic cell; return to a motif to make variation coherent.
Present a short theme, develop it through register, timing or orchestration, and make the final return feel transformed.
Keep lyrical perspective clear while instrumental texture widens or contracts around its emotional turn.
Start with a believable premise, escalate two concrete absurdities and use one reversal as the payoff instead of repeating the gag.
Treat contrasting scenes as connected dramatic acts; each major sound change needs a new cause, not arbitrary spectacle.
